stem_book: Two particles each of mass m are attached to the two ends of a light string of length L, which passes through a hole at the centre of a smooth table. One particle describes a circular path on the table with angular velocity ω₁ and the other describes a conical pendulum (string at angle θ to the vertical) with angular velocity ω₂ below the table. If ℓ₁ and ℓ₂ are the lengths of the portions of the string above and below the table, then: (a) ℓ₁/ℓ₂ = ω₂/ω₁ (b) ℓ₁/ℓ₂ = (ω₂/ω₁)² (c) 1/ω₁² + 1/ω₂² = mL/g (d) 1/ω₁² + 1/ω₂² = L cosθ/g
reason: print writes lower-case l in options (c),(d) for the total length L; corrected
work: T = mω₁²ℓ₁ = mω₂²ℓ₂ ⇒ ℓ₁/ℓ₂ = (ω₂/ω₁)²; T cosθ = mg ⇒ 1/ω₁² + 1/ω₂² = m(ℓ₁ + ℓ₂)/T = L cosθ/g
